title: Revolt-era hideouts and Byzantine church open to visitors in Judean Foothills
description: Tunnels where Jewish rebels sheltered some 2,000 years ago, alongside a Byzantine church paved with colorful mosaics, opened to the public this past weekend at Horvat Burgin in Adullam–France Park. The inauguration was a joint effort of KKL-JNF, the Israel Antiquities Authority and the Mateh Yehuda Regional Council, capping years of excavation, conservation and development. Digs led by Dr. Amir Ganor, Alon Klein and Dr. Peter Gendelman uncovered a settlement that endured from the Second Temple period through Ottoman times. Researchers suggest the large Second Temple village may be Caphar Bish, a place named by the historian Flavius Josephus. As tensions with Rome mounted in the Early Roman period, residents carved sprawling hiding networks into the bedrock. The settlement was destroyed during the Bar Kokhba Revolt of 132–136 CE. A pagan population later moved into the ruins, building anew above ground and cutting elaborate burial complexes beneath. In the Byzantine era, a church and monastery rose on the site. Dovecotes and winepresses found in the vicinity show that residents made their living from pigeon breeding, farming and winemaking. Ganor, who heads the Antiquities Authority’s Antiquities Theft Prevention Unit, described Horvat Burgin as the area’s largest ancient settlement. For years, he said, looters ravaged burial caves and tunnels and damaged standing structures. Enforcement operations, arrests of looting gangs, rescue excavations and the park’s opening finally stopped the destruction. “The site was saved,” Ganor said, “and now it can be enjoyed by the public.”

The Prime Minister's Office called the missive "an irresponsible move to publicly discuss sensitive security issues." It said all decisions were made "solely out of security considerations" and "in full coordination with the security establishment." It added that Netanyahu "once again calls on Gadi Eisenkot to join the government that is fighting terrorism," rather than "trying to form a government with supporters of terrorism," in a reference to the opposition bloc's ongoing negotiations with Arab lawmakers. In his letter, Eisenkot had cited "very worrying reports" in recent weeks about "extraneous considerations" entering "the holy of holies: Israel's security." "I demand of you: In this sensitive period, you are required to show national responsibility," the missive said. title: Congregation Kehilath Jeshurun celebrates a decade of leadership with Rabbi Chaim Steinmetz
description: Congregation Kehilath Jeshurun (KJ) will celebrate Rabbi Chaim Steinmetz’s first decade as KJ’s senior rabbi at this year’s Annual Dinner on Dec. 12. For a decade, Steinmetz has helped shape the religious and communal life of the historic Orthodox synagogue in Manhattan. His leadership has served generations of congregants, from longtime members whose families have called KJ home for decades to young professionals and families joining the community for the first time. Founded in 1872, Congregation Kehilath Jeshurun has served the Jewish community on Manhattan's Upper East Side for more than 150 years. Its community includes more than 1,200 member families and offers a broad range of religious, educational and social programming for Jews of all ages and backgrounds. Throughout his tenure, Steinmetz has helped guide the congregation as it builds upon its history while responding to the needs of contemporary Jewish life. Through his teaching, pastoral guidance and personal relationships, he has helped foster a community rooted in Torah and a shared sense of responsibility for one another. An advocate for Jews in New York City and beyond, Steinmetz also celebrated the publication of his third book, A Proud Jew , earlier this year. The Dec. 12 celebration will bring together the community Steinmetz has helped cultivate. Rather than a traditional formal dinner, the evening will feature a buffet, live music, an open bar, games and raffles. With no assigned seating, guests will have opportunities to reconnect with old friends, meet new people and celebrate together. Festive attire is encouraged. The evening will also serve as a celebration of KJ itself: the friendships, learning, traditions and acts of kindness that bring a congregation together and sustain it across generations. Whether they have belonged to KJ for decades or only recently joined the community, congregants and friends are invited to take part in the celebration and look ahead to the years to come. KJ invites the broader community to join in honoring Steinmetz on Saturday night, Dec. 12, at the Ramaz Upper School, 60 E. 78th St. Doors open at 8 p.m. To register, reserve a place or pay tribute to Steinmetz regardless of attendance, visit: ckj.org/annualdinner5787 . For questions, contact: annualdinner@ckj.org .

He said his government will take all measures "that we deem proportionate and necessary to deter any further attacks," including "those we may not disclose publicly." The goal, he said, is "to deter anyone who might be tempted, in Iran or elsewhere, to do it again." On Monday, France accused Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) of carrying out the attack last month, which made fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets heat up. Millions of euros' worth of food spoiled, and fires broke out in some stores. Barrot called the attack "unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression." title: France pressed to prove claims of Israeli online influence

The 10 most-viewed X posts from Israeli officials, government accounts, media outlets and influencers received more than 35 million views from Oct. 16 to 18, the French report said. The Combat Antisemitism (CAM) organization wrote to French Minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs Jean-Noël Barrot and Reuters CEO Steve Hasker and Editor-in-Chief Alessandra Galloni asking them to present the evidence, CAM said. “If your analysts identified factual distortions, which claims were false? If they found evidence of coordination, what was that evidence?” CAM CEO Sacha Roytman Dratwa and CAM Executive Director of European Affairs Shannon Seban wrote in their letter to Barrot. In their letter to Reuters executives, they asked why Reuters had not reported on the antisemitic conspiracy theories tied to the riots. “What I see here is a familiar conspiracy theory taking shape. Israelis comment on a crisis abroad, and the fact that people listen becomes grounds for suspecting an Israeli influence campaign,” Roytman Dratwa wrote in a statement on Monday.

title: Milan mural of Oct. 7 hostages erased
description: A leader of Italian Jews last week accused municipal authorities of “selective enforcement” after an unauthorized mural honoring Oct. 7 survivors was painted over in Milan. Walker Meghnagi, president of the Jewish Community of Milan, called the erasure a “disturbing and scandalous selectiveness” in a statement, citing dozens of examples of anti-Israel graffiti that have been allowed to remain for months. JNS reached out to the Milan municipality’s media department but received no reply by press time. "In Milan, antisemitism is out of control: Memory erased. They've whitewashed a wall, not the truth. The institutions must say which side they're on. With those who remember or those who erase," Meghnagi wrote. Italian street artist aleXsandro Palombo created the mural commemorating the Oct. 7, 2023, Hamas massacres in Israel, depicting the abduction of Israeli couple Noa Argamani and Avinatan Or from the Nova music festival. Palombo unveiled the work on the third anniversary of the attacks, on an exterior wall adjacent to Milan's Galleria d'Arte Moderna on Via Palestro, which is a municipally owned and operated museum. The black-and-white mural depicted Argamani being carried away on a motorcycle by Hamas terrorists, desperately extending her arm toward Or, whom another terrorist was leading away on foot. A large empty space separated the couple, emphasizing their forced separation and Argamani's unsuccessful attempt to reach her boyfriend. "Those who want to erase the mural want to erase October 7, just as others had attempted to erase the Holocaust. First they deny. Then they minimize. Then they erase," Meghnagi added.

title: Israel Weapon Industries, Dutch firm to produce firearms in Netherlands
description: Israel Weapon Industries (IWI) and Dutch defense company Artillerie Inrichtingen Armaments (AIA) plan to produce two IWI firearms at a new factory in the Netherlands, the companies announced on Monday. Under the planned cooperation, the Dutch company will manufacture and assemble IWI's Arad 5 rifle and the Negev UX light machine gun. IWI will provide the technology, product expertise and manufacturing know-how. AIA will set up the Dutch manufacturing operation and the infrastructure to deliver and support the weapons. The companies said the move would lay a foundation for long-term domestic production in the Netherlands. "A strong Dutch industrial base is fundamental to national security," said AIA CEO Gerard Zondervan. Ronen Hamudot, vice chairman of IWI's parent company, SK Group, said the cooperation would bring his company's "decades of experience developing and manufacturing weapon platforms for demanding operational environments into a new industrial setting." IWI is the main supplier to the Israel Defense Forces and the Israel Police. The company said its products are used in more than 60 countries.

The weapons included rifles, RPG launchers and rockets, a machine gun and fragmentation grenades. They were found alongside humanitarian aid boxes and emblems of the Amal and Hezbollah terrorist organizations, the IDF said. “This is further evidence that the UNIFIL force has failed in its mission, and of the cynical exploitation by terrorist organizations in the face of UNIFIL's inaction,” the Israeli military said in a statement. “The IDF will not allow the Hezbollah terrorist organization to harm Israeli civilians and IDF troops, and will continue operating to remove threats and remain committed to the ceasefire agreement.” UNIFIL's mandate expires on Dec. 31. Temperatures will remain unseasonably low. In Kadima, in central Israel's Sharon region, 117 millimeters (4.6 inches) of rain fell in just 75 minutes on Saturday, including approximately 100 millimeters (3.9 inches) in one hour. According to the meteorological service, the hourly total was the highest ever recorded outside Israel's coastal plain and the second-highest nationwide, behind the 110 millimeters recorded at Ma'agan Michael in November 2024. Ashdod received approximately 90 millimeters (3.5 inches) of rain, while Even Yehuda and Binyamina recorded about 70 and 50 millimeters, respectively, within an hour. Infected mosquitoes are expected to become more common every year from early June through the end of November, according to the statement. Several tests since the start of the year have turned up infected mosquitoes, it added. The ministry asked the public to drain standing water, use repellent and install window screens. Dr. Shai Reicher, head of the ministry's Pests and Pest Control Department, said this autumn has had "relatively warm and dry weather, which allows suitable living conditions for the development of mosquitoes."
